payload_identity: A shard header records NO token-payload digest (fields: data_snapshot_hash, tokenizer_hash, remap_hash, counts, buckets, code_fingerprint, corpus_rev, sequence_index_hash, ...; tokens.u32 is only length-checked). The data-level identity it does record is data_snapshot_hash, the hash of the corpus snapshot the rows were drawn from. Both guards refuse a header whose data_snapshot_hash is one of the retired ones, so a re-hashed copy, or a rebuild from the same snapshot under drifted code (which gets a new shard_hash), is refused too. Checked on all 89 headers of AUDIT/x4-v1-headers-2026-10-22/sets.json: only the three sets above carry these two snapshot hashes; the v6 sets carry 1d33e7da... (train) and 3743996d... (val). Limit: a set rebuilt from a DIFFERENT snapshot of the same sources is not identified by this key; the pipeline-level refusal (real_tokenizer_pipeline under --rev 8e6a00952a09e31a09cc3f5270229a935b7235cc with the v5 rule) is not added here because tools/real_tokenizer_pipeline.py is outside this lane's files.

enforcement.python: python/qd_train/artifacts.py ShardHeader.from_json, after the shard_hash verification: refuses a header whose shard_hash or data_snapshot_hash is retired. ShardReader parses the header before assert_shard_trainable, so allow_stale_code does not reach it.
enforcement.rust: crates/qd-train/src/shards.rs ShardHeader::from_json (the header reader qd-train and qd-train-metal share): refuses the recorded shard_hash, the derived shard_hash and the data_snapshot_hash, before the shard_hash comparison.

not_covered: A tool that json.loads header.json or np.loads tokens.u32 without either header parser is not stopped; neither is a v5r-snapshot set whose header was edited to another data_snapshot_hash and re-hashed (a forgery; the sequence_index would still name the same rows).
